key_insight: An evidence-based GPT-5 workflow showed promising prospective prediction of clinical trial outcomes, rather than cancer drug discovery specifically.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support trial research prioritization, but does not establish treatment efficacy or guide individual patient care.
method: TrialDossier assembles standardized dossiers from public evidence.
TrialOutlook uses GPT-5 to estimate whether trials will meet prespecified primary endpoints.
Fixed forecasts are linked to subsequently disclosed, adjudicated outcomes.
evidence_signal: Among 69 adjudicated outcomes from 694 ongoing trials, AUROC was 0.819 (95% CI, 0.708–0.914) and average precision was 0.860; 27 of 29 failures were identified, but 17 of 40 successes were classified as failures.
watch_item: Only 69 outcomes were adjudicated, and the substantial misclassification of successful trials warrants caution before operational use.
paper_title: Prospective prediction of clinical trial outcomes from public evidence
